releases.name: Installers v1.4.41
releases.body:
Wakeshift's installers, version 2026.11.10.0730+cab6abc. Its source is this repository at ec2724e30f982b6f1c7374fa0e3f039a1716b76b, exported from wakeshift/wakeshift@cab6abcc8cee.

Install for your agent (for example Codex): `curl -fsSL https://github.com/wakeshift/connectors/releases/latest/download/codex.sh | sh`.
Each script carries the SHA-256 of what it downloads from this release and refuses anything else.

The `wakeshift-connect-*.tgz`, `wakeshift-opencode-*.tgz`, `wakeshift-pi-*.tgz` and `wakeshift-openclaw-*.tgz` files are this release's npm packages (`@wakeshift/connect`, its platform packages, `@wakeshift/opencode`, `@wakeshift/pi` and `@wakeshift/openclaw`), published to npm from here with provenance.

To check a release by hand, with [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/system_config/installation/):

```sh
cosign verify-blob --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity 'https://github.com/wakeshift/wakeshift/.github/workflows/installers.yml@refs/tags/v1.4.41' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```

releases.name: @wakeshift/cli 0.1.4
releases.body: - **`init`'s console link ends in `?ref=cli`** before its fragment, so Wakeshift can count accounts that start from the CLI. Sign-in saves the tag on the new account and nowhere else; the key stays in the fragment. This was listed under 0.1.3, which was released without it.

releases.name: @wakeshift/cli 0.1.3
releases.body: - **`init` says plainly when you're on Wakeshift's waitlist**, and exits 3: "You're on Wakeshift's waitlist, so the app wasn't created. Wakeshift will email you when your account is ready; run init again then (it keeps the key in .env)." Wakeshift now answers the link's key with `403 waitlisted` once the waitlist page has seen the link, so `init` stops at once instead of waiting 10 minutes and timing out (earlier versions exit 3 there too, with Wakeshift's own message).
